answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a fixed period before it can earn reputation or influence, then slash that stake if independent audits show coordinated deception. A real entrant pays an opportunity cost and risks honest capital, but a sybil operator must fund every persona separately and keep funds immobilized; copying names is cheap, multiplying credible identities is not. The jade account may wander into a violet group, but its bond still has to stand behind its claims.
